verdict.rationale: For a local package manager, the user's data is the project manifest and lockfile. Bun keeps dependencies in standard npm-compatible `package.json` and uses a readable text-based `bun.lock`. It can also write a Yarn v1 lockfile alongside it (`bun install --yarn`), so a project can move to another client. A community member says switching costs nothing because Bun can be used purely as a package manager. Missing for 10: export to npm `package-lock.json` or pnpm lockfile formats, a first-party migration-away guide, and independent hands-on confirmation of leaving Bun for another client.
